title: The Uneven Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Entrepreneurial Performance: Evidence from a Field Experiment in Kenya
authors: Nicholas G. Otis; Rowan Philip Clarke; Solène Delecourt; David Holtz; Rembrand Michael Koning
eligible_reason: Randomized field experiment, not a staggered adoption design. Kenyan entrepreneurs are randomized once into AI-assistant vs. control (Rand == 'AI'); main estimates are lm_robust ATE regressions of post-treatment performance on the treatment indicator plus post-double-selection lasso covariates and block FE, clustered by entrepreneur, with heterogeneity by baseline performance (GEmed99/GEmed95). The DiD variant (UIC_DID) stacks the baseline and the post-treatment average into two periods with (Rand == 'AI') x Post_Treatment, a single common treatment date. One adoption cohort; lasso-selected controls in every column.
design_notes: R (estimatr lm_robust). 05_MainAnalysis.R produces Table 1, Figure 2 and appendix Tables A1-A3; 06_TextAnalysis.R produces Tables 2-5 (text data not shipped). UICL.rda is the entrepreneur-by-survey long panel.
data_files_note: Main-analysis survey data shipped (cleaned and raw); chat/text data withheld for confidentiality.
screener_notes: No article text; abstract from OpenAlex frame.
